definition: Isotopes are variants of an element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons; the atomic mass number is protons plus neutrons, while the atomic number is protons alone.
core_idea: Isotopes of an element behave identically chemically but differ in nuclear stability due to differing atomic weight; the number after an element's chemical symbol (e.g., U-235, U-238) denotes the atomic mass number (protons + neutrons), distinct from the atomic number (protons only), which is not shown in a chemical formula.
key_points: Isotopes share the same proton count but differ in neutron count.
Chemically, isotopes of the same element behave identically.
Nuclear stability differs between isotopes because of differing atomic weight.
The number appended to a chemical symbol (e.g., U-238, U-235) is the atomic mass number: protons + neutrons combined.
Protons and neutrons weigh about the same, but only protons carry electrical charge.
The atomic number is the count of protons in the nucleus and is never explicitly shown in a chemical formula.
relationships: Distinguishes U-235 from U-238 in the enrichment process
caveats: The number after an element's symbol (mass number) is sometimes mistaken for the atomic number; the source explicitly distinguishes the two.
